Applications are invited for a fully funded doctoral project "AI-Powered Collaboration in Flexible Teams”, under my supervision at University College Cork, Ireland.

AI-Powered Collaboration in Flexible Teams - with Professor Luigina Colfi (School of Applied Psychology, contact:

). A qualitative investigation of evolving cooperation patterns in flexible work and the role of AI-powered tools and systems in how teams plan and enact coordination practices across time and locations.

For this project, we particularly welcome applicants with background and/or knowledge in, but not limited to: human-computer interaction, computer-supported cooperative work, work and organisational studies, qualitative research methods.

Context:

Rinn Artificial Intelligence is designed to serve as a national hub for research and innovation in data science and AI. The programme has two overarching goals: (i) to advance foundational cutting-edge research in Data Science and AI, and (ii) to pursue open, international, and inter- and transdisciplinary research aimed at studying, designing, and implementing strategies to address societal challenges.

As part of Rinn Artificial Intelligence applications are invited for a cohort of 19 PhD studentships within University College Cork’s Futures for Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics.

These studentships are available through a cohort-based PhD training programme across a suite of research themes: foundational methods, translational methods, data & processing, people-centred AI, democratic governance, society & culture and health. Applications are sought from a broad range of graduates in arts & humanities, business and education, computer science, engineering, health sciences, life science & environment, mathematics & statistics and social science & law.

Alongside their individual PhD research, students will benefit from a structured, cohort-based PhD training programme. This programme will include transferable skills training (e.g., communication skills, ethics, and entrepreneurship), group activities (e.g., hackathons and spin-out sprints), training on domain-specific topics (e.g., machine learning, statistics, data management, programming, qualitative and digital policy methods), and peer-led learning opportunities (e.g., research seminars, peer-designed workshops, and reading groups). Dedicated career and skills development activities will also be offered.

Students will benefit from extensive engagement with industry and public service partners and from an enrichment experience e.g., industry training placements, an academic research visit to an internationally renowned collaborating institution, or other similar activities. This experience will equip graduates with the knowledge and skills necessary to thrive in academia, industry, and public service.

Funding:

Studentships provide a stipend of €25,000 per year for four years (tax free) with additional funds available to support e.g., equipment, conference attendance, and training activities. Fees for EU students will be covered automatically, while non-EU students will receive a fee waiver from University College Cork.

Applications:

Interested applicants should apply here:

and indicate the Research Theme "Research Theme: Human-AI Collaboration & Cognition”, the Supervisor Name “Luigina Ciolfi” and the host institution “University College Cork” in the appropriate places in the form.

The cover letter should outline the applicant's motivation in applying for the project and how the applicant envisions making the project their own.

Application Process:

We are committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) and particularly encourage applications from under-represented groups. We are currently recruiting for the October 2026 intake. Applications are open and will be reviewed on a fortnightly basis until all positions have been filled. Due to the short timeline, the Supervisor recommends applying no later than 02 July 2026.

Due to the large number of applications received, only applicants invited to interview will receive an email response. Please note that applicants who are invited to interview and are successful, will have to subsequently apply to the host institution inline with their requirements.

Informal queries about this doctoral project can be sent directly to Professor Luigina Ciolfi at
Enquiries about Rinn Artificial Intelligence or general questions about this process may be directed to Professor Barry O’Sullivan (Rinn AI Institutional Lead at UCC) - osullivan.barry@ucc.ie
